title: Minimum Capacity Subset
prompt:
Implement `best_capacity_subset(properties, group_size, neighborhood=None) -> list[dict]`. Each property is a mapping with a nonnegative integer `capacity` and may have a `neighborhood`. When `neighborhood` is supplied, only properties whose neighborhood equals it are eligible. Return a subset of the original property mappings whose total capacity is at least `group_size`.

Rank feasible subsets by `(total_capacity, property_count, original_index_tuple)` and return the chosen original mappings in their input order. Thus, minimize excess capacity first, then the number of properties, then use original input positions only as a final deterministic tie-breaker. Return `[]` when no eligible subset is feasible; `group_size == 0` also returns `[]`. Do not mutate the input mappings or reorder the returned objects.

The eligible list is small enough for subset search or backtracking. Capacities are nonnegative, which makes capacity-based pruning safe. Aim for O(2^n * n) worst-case time and O(n) auxiliary space, excluding the returned list.

example.reasoning: Capacity ten is preferred to the single-property alternative with capacity eleven.
